What the
Ecosystem Delivers
FY 2025–26 marked another year of strong, broad-based 
expansion for Zaggle. We delivered consolidated revenue of 
₹1,908 crore, growing 46% year-on-year, while profit growth 
outpaced revenue growth, reflecting the increasing operating 
leverage of our SaaS-fintech platform. This performance was 
supported by a growing enterprise base, deeper engagement 
with existing customers and the continued expansion of our 
product and partner ecosystem.
Zaggle enters FY 2026–27 from a position of 
strength, having established leadership in India’s 
spend management category and built the 
scale, capabilities and ecosystem to unlock its 
next phase of growth.
Our ecosystem today brings together 
3,915+ corporate customers and 
3.9 million active users, supported 
by relationships with 19 leading 
banking partners and the three 
major payment networks — 
Visa, Mastercard and RuPay. 
These partnerships provide the 
distribution, payment infrastructure 
and financial rails that enable us to 
serve enterprises and their wider 
stakeholder networks at scale.
Growth during the year was not 
limited to adding new customers; 
it increasingly came from 
deepening our relationships with 
existing enterprises. Customers 
are progressively moving beyond 
individual use cases to adopt multiple 
solutions across employee benefits, 
expense management, procurement, 
incentives, payments and analytics. 
This land-and-expand model 
strengthens platform engagement 
while creating opportunities to 
increase revenue from the same 
enterprise relationship.
The quality of this growth is reflected 
in our retention metrics. Customer 
churn remained below 1.5% during 
FY 2025–26, demonstrating the 
stickiness of our platform and the 
value created as customers embed 
Zaggle deeper into their financial 
workflows. At the same time, 
disciplined customer acquisition and 
an expanding addressable market 
have enabled us to scale without 
compromising operating efficiency.
Our strategic acquisitions during 
the year further strengthened this 
ecosystem. GreenEdge expanded 
our capabilities in loyalty, rewards 
and experiential engagement, with 
its integration creating opportunities 
to introduce these offerings across 
our broader enterprise network. 
Rivpe Technology Private Limited, 
now Zagg.Money, marked another 
significant evolution of our platform 
by extending our B2B2C model 
into consumer financial services 
and opening a new monetisation 
opportunity across our existing 
salaried-user base.

Efficient and Resilient
Building a More
Growth Engine
Scale alone does not define the strength of an ecosystem. 
What matters is the ability to convert scale into stronger 
economics, deeper customer relationships and sustain-
able long-term value.
During FY 2025–26, Zaggle continued 
to strengthen the quality of its growth 
by sharpening its revenue mix and 
improving the economics of its platform. 
The Company’s expanding ecosystem is 
enabling greater operating leverage, with 
profit growth outpacing revenue growth 
during the year.
The evolution of the Propel business 
illustrates this approach. As the platform 
scaled, Zaggle continued to refine its 
programme economics, with the incentive-
to-programme-fee ratio moderating from 
71% to approximately 65–66%, with a long-
term objective of reaching a more efficient 
steady-state level of around 50%. This 
creates a meaningful pathway for improved 
profitability as a greater proportion of 
programme revenue is retained within the 
business.
The focus, therefore, is not simply on 
maximising transaction volumes, but on 
improving the quality of every transaction 
flowing through the platform. As the 
ecosystem expands, increasing scale, 
deeper product adoption and a more 
favourable revenue mix have the potential 
to strengthen operating leverage and 
enhance long-term cash generation.
This disciplined approach to growth 
has also been reinforced by continued 
confidence in Zaggle’s long-term 
opportunity. During the year, RAN Ventures 
Private Limited, the promoter group, and 
Bennett Coleman and Company Limited, 
non promoter (Times Group) subscribed 
to warrants at ₹567 per share, reflecting 
confidence in the Company’s strategy, 
platform and future growth potential.
The result is an ecosystem designed not merely to 
become larger, but to become progressively stronger as it 
scales. With this foundation in place, the next chapter of 
the story lies in the new capabilities and growth avenues 
being added to the platform.

How the Ecosystem
Expanded
Three new layers came to life this year, each one opening 
a market that the platform could serve for the first time.
The first is consumer finance. Zaggle already 
serves 3.9 million salaried users through its 
corporate platform. This year, the Company 
began offering those users credit, lending, 
and insurance products directly at near-zero 
acquisition cost because the customers are 
already within the platform. An 8-week pilot 
acquired 36,000 to 40,000 cards. Credit Line 
on UPI processed over 30 lakh transactions 
and disbursed more than ₹50 crore in its 
first quarter. The fourth monetisation pillar 
is live, and it already has numbers behind it.
The second is embedded intelligence. 
Zaggle deployed Agentic AI into live 
production this year. Invoice reconciliation 
that runs autonomously. Real-time policy 
enforcement at the point of spend. The 
impact is already measurable: feature 
launch times have been reduced by 50%, 
and bill-processing turnaround has been 
cut by more than 80%. The platform now 
builds faster than the market can ask.
The third is international reach. Zaggle 
Payments IFSC Limited in GIFT City, 
establishing a dedicated platform for 
cross-border financial services. UAE 
has been identified as the Company’s 
hub for the MENA region, supported by 
engagement with senior stakeholders as 
Zaggle evaluates opportunities across the 
region. The Company is also preparing for 
entry into the US market towards the end 
of FY 2026-27, with its technology and 
compliance architecture being localised to 
meet the requirements of the market.
Subsequent to FY 2025–26, Zaggle further 
strengthened its international payments 
capabilities through the acquisition of a 
19.9% stake in Unobanc Private Limited, 
adding regulated foreign-exchange 
capabilities and further strengthening the 
architecture supporting its cross-border 
payments strategy.
This positioning gives Zaggle multiple 
gateways into international markets-
GIFT City as the cross-border financial 
infrastructure hub, UAE as the MENA 
springboard, and the US as a longer-term 
growth opportunity.
The platform now spans corporate spend, 
consumer finance, artificial intelligence, 
and cross-border payments. What remains 
is what it will deliver, and the commitments 
that make delivery measurable.

STATEMENT FROM THE EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN’S DESK
“We set out to 
build a new way 
for enterprises to 
manage spend.

is taking shape 
as an integrated

built around

When we began Zaggle, India’s 
enterprise spending landscape was 
largely fragmented. Businesses relied 
on a combination of reimbursement 
processes, corporate cards, 
standalone rewards programmes 
and manual financial workflows. We 
saw an opportunity to bring these 
disparate elements together and 
create a technology-led platform 
that could make enterprise spending 
more visible, controlled and 
intelligent.
Over the years, that vision has 
evolved into a comprehensive 
SaaS-fintech ecosystem spanning 
employee expenses and benefits, 
procurement and vendor payments, 
channel incentives and rewards, 
spend analytics, international 
payments and consumer financial 
services. 
Our progress is not defined by 
scale alone. It is defined by the 
increasing number of ways in which 
our platform can create value for 
the enterprises and stakeholders 
connected to it. A customer may 
begin with one use case and 
subsequently extend Zaggle across 
multiple aspects of its financial 
operations. This ability to deepen 
relationships is central to the platform 
we are building.
Building Through 
Complementary Capabilities
Our approach to expansion has 
always been guided by a simple 
principle: every new capability should 
strengthen the ecosystem around it.
During FY 2025–26, GreenEdge 
expanded our capabilities in 
loyalty, rewards and experiential 
engagement, while Rivpe Technology 
Private Limited, now Zagg.
Money, opened a new avenue by 
extending our reach from enterprise 
relationships into consumer financial 
services. These businesses bring 
complementary capabilities to 
the Zaggle ecosystem and create 
opportunities to leverage our existing 
distribution, technology and user 
base in new ways.
Our acquisition philosophy remains 
focused on strategic fit rather than 
scale for its own sake. We evaluate 
whether a capability can strengthen 
an existing platform layer, open a new 
monetisation opportunity or create 
access to an adjacent market. This 
discipline will remain important as we 
continue to evaluate opportunities 
for inorganic growth.
Artificial Intelligence: From 
Technology to Transformation
Artificial intelligence is becoming an 
increasingly important part of this 
evolution.
For Zaggle, AI is not simply a 
technology layer added to existing 
products. We are embedding 
intelligence into how our platform is 
built, operated and experienced by 
customers. Our Agentic AI initiatives 
are designed to automate complex 
workflows, including reconciliation, 
compliance monitoring and financial 
processes that have traditionally 
required significant manual 
intervention.
The impact is already visible in 
our operating environment. AI-led 
engineering has helped reduce 
product feature development 
timelines, while automation 
has significantly shortened bill-
processing turnaround times. More 
importantly, these capabilities are 
creating the foundation for a platform 
that can become faster, more 
adaptive and increasingly intelligent 
as its scale expands.
The acquisition of AI capabilities 
and talent through DICE in FY 2027 
is another step in this journey. 
We believe the combination of 
proprietary technology, specialised 
talent and the data generated 
through our enterprise ecosystem 
can become an important source of 
differentiation as we build for the 
next phase of growth.
Trust Is the Foundation of Scale
Technology creates possibilities; trust 
makes them scalable.
Our long-standing relationships with 
Visa, Mastercard and RuPay, together 
with our network of 19 banking 
partners, demonstrate the depth 
of institutional relationships that 
underpin Zaggle’s business. These 
partnerships enable us to combine 
our technology with established 
financial infrastructure and deliver 
solutions to enterprises at scale.
Our A-; Stable credit rating from CARE 
further reflects the strengthening 
institutional profile of the Company. 
We continue to invest in governance, 
risk management, data security 
and regulatory compliance as the 
platform expands across products 
and geographies.
For us, governance is not separate 
from growth. It is an essential part 
of building a financial technology 
platform that enterprises, banking 
partners, employees and investors 
can rely on for the long term.
An Indian Platform with Global 
Ambitions
The next phase of Zaggle’s journey 
extends beyond India.
The establishment of Zaggle 
Payments IFSC Limited in GIFT City 
provides an important foundation 
for our international payments 
strategy. We have also identified 
UAE as our hub for the MENA region, 
supported by engagement with 
senior stakeholders in the UAE as we 
evaluate opportunities across the 
region.
Our international ambition is 
underpinned by the same principles 
that shaped our domestic platform: 
technology, regulatory understanding 
and strong partnerships. As we 
prepare for eventual entry into 
markets such as the United States, 
our focus is on ensuring that the 
platform is appropriately localised for 
each market, including its compliance 
architecture and AI capabilities.
This is more than a geographic 
expansion. It is an opportunity to take 
F
ellow Stakeholders,
an enterprise technology platform 
developed in India and apply its 
capabilities to increasingly complex 
global financial workflows.
The Zaggle Brand
As our platform expands from 
enterprise spend management into 
a broader financial ecosystem, our 
brand is evolving alongside it.
The appointment of Ayush Mhatre 
as our brand ambassador represents 
this evolution. As captain of the 
India Under-19 cricket team, an 
India A player, a Mumbai Ranji 
Trophy representative and a Chennai 
Super Kings player in the IPL, Ayush 
embodies ambition, energy and the 
potential of a new generation.
His association with Zaggle has also 
brought the brand into a broader 
national conversation. His U19 World 
Cup campaign, with the Zaggle 
brand prominently visible on his bat, 
provided an important moment of 
visibility for the Company as we build 
recognition beyond our traditional 
enterprise audience.
As we develop Zagg.Money and 
expand our consumer-facing 
offerings, this growing brand 
recognition will become increasingly 
relevant to how we engage with 
the next generation of financial 
consumers.
Looking Ahead
The opportunity before Zaggle 
is significant. We are operating 
in a market where enterprise 
digitisation, embedded finance, AI 
and digital payments are converging 
to fundamentally reshape how 
businesses manage money.
Our focus is therefore not on 
pursuing growth at any cost, but on 
building an increasingly complete, 
intelligent and scalable enterprise 
finance platform. We will continue to 
deepen our presence with existing 
customers, expand our product 
ecosystem, integrate complementary 
capabilities and selectively enter 
new markets where our technology 
and operating model can create 
differentiated value.
Over the medium to long term, we 
see the potential for Zaggle to build 
a business supported by a stronger 
mix of recurring and transaction-led 
revenues and a sustainable 14–15% 
adjusted EBITDA margin. This is an 
ambition that reflects the scale of 
the opportunity ahead rather than a 
near-term forecast.
The foundation for that opportunity 
has been built over more than a 
decade. The next phase will be about 
converting that foundation into 
greater scale, stronger economics 
and a broader global presence while 
remaining anchored in the principles 
that have guided Zaggle from the 
beginning.
We have built the platform. We 
are now focused on expanding its 
possibilities.
W
arm regards,
Dr. Raj P. Narayanam
Executive Chairman

Why We Restructured DICE
Every acquisition Zaggle has 
completed in the past two years 
followed the same principle: will this 
asset multiply inside the platform, 
or will it simply sit alongside it? That 
principle was tested most rigorously 
with DICE, with the transaction 
completing in FY 2026-27.
The original transaction was 
structured as a share purchase. As 
our diligence deepened, the team 
identified a more precise path. The 
technology suite, the intellectual 
property, and the product contracts 
all sat within an asset perimeter that 
could be carved out and absorbed 
directly onto the standalone profit 
and loss statement. The result was 
a materially lower outlay, a cleaner 
integration, and something equally 
important: the people- the AI 
engineers, the product architects, the 
compliance specialists- joined Zaggle 
because they chose to, because they 
saw what the platform could become 
with their contribution.
What the Platform Delivered 
Financially
Adjusted EBITDA reached ₹192 crore 
for the year, a 51% expansion over  
FY 2024–25. Profit after tax reached 
₹139 crore, a 52% expansion. Both 
grew meaningfully faster than 
revenue, which expanded at 46%. 
That gap between top-line and 
bottom-line growth is the platform’s 
operating leverage at work. As 
more clients transact across more 
products on a shared infrastructure, 
the incremental cost of serving each 
transaction falls, revenue scales 
ahead of the cost base, and the 
margin widens with every additional 
rupee earned.
How We Are Building the 
Intelligence Layer
Profitability at this pace demands 
an engine underneath it, and that 
engine is the intelligence layer.
Integrating over a hundred AI 
professionals into an existing 
engineering culture is as much 
an organisational challenge as a 
technical one. We rebuilt team 
structures, harmonised development 
frameworks, and embedded a single 
engineering culture across what were 
previously independent product 
organisations. The development 
cycle, which historically took more 
than 75 days to deliver a new feature, 
has already been compressed to 
under 30 days. We have set a target 
of reducing it several notches lower. 
That target is ambitious, and I am 
committed to reaching it.
The intelligence layer is what 
transforms the platform from a 
transaction processor into a decision 
engine. Every reconciliation that runs 
autonomously, every policy enforced 
in real time, every tax flag raised 
before the deadline, adds a layer of 
value that a simple payments product 
cannot match. This is the difference 
between processing spend and 
managing it.
The Path to Self-Funding Growth
The profitability trajectory is 
established. The next milestone is 
converting that profitability into 
positive operating cash flow, the 
point at which the business funds its 
own growth from its own operations.
The path involves three things 
working together: the incentive ratio 
continuing to compress, the Propel 
redemption model completing its 
transition, and trade receivable cycles 
tightening as the enterprise client 
base matures. Each is underway. Each 
is being tracked at the management 
committee level.
What We Intend to Achieve
The ZAGG.money retail offering will 
move from pilot to full-scale rollout 
during the year. We will also advance 
our MENA expansion, building on the 
UAE and GIFT City entity established 
this past year. These are commitments 
stated in a public document. We 
expect to be measured against them.
The same rigour governs how we 
set external guidance. We guide 
conservatively because we believe 
the credibility earned by consistently 
exceeding stated targets is worth 
more than the momentary attention 
earned by setting aggressive ones. 
Positive operating cash flow matters 
more to this management team than 
another quarter of headline revenue 
acceleration.
The Platform We Are Building
What I want to leave you with is this. 
The platform we have assembled- 
payments, software, rewards, 
intelligence, consumer finance, cross-
border infrastructure- is more than 
a product suite. It is a compounding 
system where each layer reinforces 
the layers around it, and each client 
who enters deepens the data. 
Each capability we add widens the 
distance between Zaggle and any 
competitor attempting to replicate 
what has been built.
The willingness to under-promise, the 
patience to let compounding do its 
work, and the resolve to over-deliver 
on every commitment we make 
publicly are the temperament that 
will sustain this journey. It is the one 
thing I will always protect.
Thank you for your continued trust 
and belief in our vision.
W
arm regards
Avinash Ramesh Godkhindi
Managing Director and Chief 
Executive Officer

ABOUT ZAGGLE PREPAID
Zaggle is where
Finance Meets Foresight.
We are one of India’s leading SaaS-led fintech platforms, transforming how enterprises 
manage, automate and optimise business spending.
Who We Are
Our Mission
Our Values
Founded in 2011 by Dr. Raj P. Narayanam, Zaggle began 
with a single conviction: that the way Indian corporates 
managed spending was fundamentally broken and that 
technology could fix it. What started as a prepaid card 
business has evolved into an integrated enterprise finance 
platform that brings together software, payments and 
financial intelligence on a single digital architecture.
Today, Zaggle operates a B2B2C model that connects 
enterprises with their employees, vendors, suppliers, 
dealers, channel partners and financial institutions 
through one unified ecosystem. The platform is built on 
a cloud-native, API-first architecture that integrates with 
existing ERP, HRMS, CRM and banking systems, enabling 
organisations to digitise financial workflows without 
replacing the infrastructure they already operate.
To build state-of-the-art FinTech solutions, workflows 
and products which would help automate and empower 
businesses to increase efficiency, accuracy, transparency, 
and productivity and which would eventually help India 
achieve the goal of becoming a digital economy.
Our core values lie in uplifting the customer’s experience 
through simple and efficient products.
Innovation: Creativity fuels everything we do. We go the 
extra mile to create innovative products that redefine user 
experiences.
Customer-Centric: We are customer-obsessed, and they 
are the basic foundation for us.
Excellence: We believe in excellence as a way of life, and 
quality is our highest priority.
Empathy: We engage with all stakeholders with empathy 
and attempt, at all times, to assess situations by looking at 
it from the other person/entities perspective as well.
Security: We maintain high-security standards for all our 
customers’ data and information.
Sustainability: We are dedicated to building a sustainable 
future for the FinTech industry and bringing in a positive 
impact among the people.
Reliability: We are consistent in delivering the most 
reliable products for our customers.
Transparency: We are committed to maintaining two-way 
and open communication with users.
Continuous Improvement: We work relentlessly to 
improve and remain at the cutting edge of technology.

Zoyer
ACCOUNTS PAYABLE AND VENDOR PAYMENT AUTOMATION
Zoyer is Zaggle’s flagship platform for digitising and controlling how enterprises 
pay their vendors. It brings invoice capture, multi-level approval workflows, 
automated reconciliation and vendor onboarding into a single system, replacing 
the fragmented, manual accounts payable processes that still dominate most 
Indian enterprises.
A key sub-module, BROME (Branch Recurring Operating Monthly Expenses), 
addresses a problem specific to distributed businesses: recurring branch-level 
costs such as petty cash, utility payments and rentals. Through QR and UPI-
enabled payment infrastructure and BBPS integration via NPCI and Yes BANK, 
BROME allows retail chains, logistics companies and financial services businesses 
to automate utility bill fetching, manage multi-level approval workflows and 
reconcile payments against ERP records, all from a central dashboard. The result 
is tighter compliance, uniform controls and the elimination of small leakages that 
compound across hundreds of locations.
Zoyer has grown into one of the most significant contributors to the business, 
proof that solving a genuinely difficult enterprise problem at scale compounds 
faster than incremental feature development. A leading quick-service restaurant 
chain uses Zoyer’s QR-enabled petty cash module across its outlet network. A 
major healthcare and diagnostics chain expanded from Save into Zoyer across 
more than 130 clinics. A prominent skin and wellness clinic chain adopted the 
BBPS utility bill automation to centralise branch-level payments. More recently, a 
leading insurance company onboarded Zoyer under a multi-year agreement, and 
an existing FMCG client expanded its Zoyer engagement further, underscoring 
the platform’s pull into new verticals beyond our original enterprise base.
Save
EMPLOYEE EXPENSE AND BENEFITS MANAGEMENT
Save is the module that anchors Zaggle’s relationship with the individual 
employee. It streamlines expense reimbursements, manages tax-advantaged 
benefits and disburses allowances through co-branded prepaid cards and 
a mobile-first interface: meal cards, fuel cards, travel reimbursements and 
corporate benefits, all governed by configurable policy engines.
Where traditional reimbursement cycles in Indian enterprises can stretch 
from 5 to 35 days, Save compresses this to a matter of hours and minutes. 
Administrators gain granular controls over usage and real-time visibility into 
spend, while employees gain a simplified, transparent way to claim and track 
their own expenses. Save integrates seamlessly with payroll systems, making 
it both a retention tool for enterprise clients and a source of recurring, sticky 
revenue for Zaggle.
Propel
CHANNEL INCENTIVES, REWARDS AND LOYALTY 
MANAGEMENT
Propel digitises how enterprises design, deploy and monitor incentive 
programmes for their dealers, distributors and channel partners. It 
supports instant payouts through cards or digital vouchers, offers 125+ 
redemption options and provides performance analytics dashboards that 
give clients real-time visibility into programme effectiveness.
Propel now contributes the majority share of total revenue, a milestone 
that reflects both the platform’s scale and the trust large enterprises place 
in it to manage sales-driven, performance-linked incentive structures. 
With the integration of GreenEdge, Propel’s rewards ecosystem now 
extends into specialised, premium loyalty experiences including golf-
based corporate engagement, deepening the platform’s appeal for 
enterprises seeking to reward and retain their highest-value relationships.

ZIP - Zaggle 
International Payments
SIMPLIFYING GLOBAL TRANSACTIONS
As Indian enterprises increasingly operate across borders, ZIP addresses 
the complexity of cross-border spend with live foreign exchange rates

platform also allows businesses to segregate business and personal forex

ZIP is the transactional infrastructure that underpins Zaggle’s international 
expansion. As the Company builds out its cross-border operations, this 
same international payments architecture will support Indian enterprises 
transacting globally and, over time, international clients as well.
ZatiX
AI-BASED INTELLIGENT SPEND 
ANALYTICS
ZatiX represents Zaggle’s shift from transaction processing to 
genuine financial intelligence. Offered as part of a bundled 
solution alongside corporate credit cards, ZatiX gives CFOs 
and finance teams predictive insights, spend benchmarking 
and optimisation recommendations grounded in real, live data 
rather than quarterly hindsight. This is the clearest expression 
of the broader AI strategy: helping enterprises move beyond 
recording what they spent toward understanding what they 
should spend next, and why.
TaxSpanner
TAX PREPARATION, COMPLIANCE AND EMPLOYEE 
FINANCIAL WELLNESS
TaxSpanner brings professional-grade tax preparation and filing 
capabilities directly into the Zaggle ecosystem, extending the value 
proposition from expense management into genuine financial wellness 
for the employees the platform already serves. The module supports 
TDS filing for enterprise vendors via Zoyer, individual tax returns 
for employees via Save, and tax compliance for agents, dealers and 
distributors via Propel, creating natural cross-sell pathways across the 
platform.
Fleet Spend Management
SIMPLIFYING GLOBAL TRANSACTIONS
Purpose-built for enterprises managing transportation and logistics operations, 
the fleet solution provides fuel card issuance, granular spend controls and real-
time monitoring through dashboards tailored for fleet owners, oil marketing 
companies and CNG providers. Advanced spend controls and automated 
approval workflows enable administrators to set transaction-level limits 
and generate trip-level analytics, addressing one of the largest historically 
uncontrolled expense lines for logistics-intensive businesses.
The Driver Wallet concept allows corporates to push funds from the corporate 
wallet into individual driver wallets, restricting spend to OEM-authorised service 
centres and approved fuel stations. Torrent Gas operates on this model, using 
Zaggle’s fleet platform to manage CNG fleet spend with full audit trail visibility.
With India’s trucking and logistics economy continuing to formalise and digitise, 
this module positions Zaggle to capture a large, underpenetrated adjacent 
market well beyond the traditional enterprise client base.
Prepaid, Corporate Credit and 
Forex Cards
THE PHYSICAL AND DIGITAL RAILS BENEATH EVERY SOLUTION
At the foundation of Zaggle’s entire ecosystem lies the card issuance 
infrastructure. With over 50 million cards issued to date, Zaggle holds its 
position as India’s largest prepaid card issuer, built on partnerships spanning 
19 banks and all three major global card networks: Visa, Mastercard and RuPay.
This year, the infrastructure expanded further with the Zaggle GlobalPay Forex 
Card, strengthening the international spend suite. Whether it is an employee 
benefit disbursed through Save, a vendor payment processed through Zoyer, 
an incentive redeemed through Propel, or a fuel spend managed through 
Fleet, every transaction ultimately flows through this card infrastructure, 
making it the connective rail across the entire platform.

BACK-END TECHNOLOGY 
The Technology 
Behind The Intelligence
Technology has always been the foundation of Zaggle’s business, but FY 2025–26 marked the beginning of a 
new chapter. The platform is evolving from cloud-native spend management into an AI-native enterprise finance 
architecture where automation, intelligence and embedded financial infrastructure work together across every stage of 
enterprise spending.
API-First Integration Architecture
Security, Compliance and 
Platform Trust
Mobile-First Interfaces
Agentic AI in Enterprise Finance
The platform is fully API-enabled, allowing seamless plug-
and-play integration with enterprise ERP, HRMS, CRM, 
accounting and banking systems. Organisations adopt 
Zaggle without replacing the infrastructure they already 
operate. Implementation cycles are shorter, onboarding is 
faster and enterprises can scale adoption across multiple 
business functions with minimal disruption.
This architecture is what makes modular product 
adoption possible. When a client adds a second or third 
solution to its Zaggle deployment, the integration work 
takes days rather than weeks because the API layer has 
already connected the platform to the client’s operating 
environment.
With financial operations at the heart of the platform, 
compliance and security are foundational. The 
infrastructure is designed around enterprise-grade 
security controls, continuous vulnerability assessments, 
penetration testing and secure software development 
practices.
The platform adheres to internationally recognised 
standards including GDPR, ISO 27001, PCI DSS and 
AICPA SOC 2, while maintaining full compliance with 
RBI mandates governing prepaid payment instruments, 
digital payments and data privacy. These frameworks 
ensure secure, resilient and auditable financial operations 
for enterprises, banking partners and millions of platform 
users.
Every interaction point on the platform is engineered 
with a mobile-first design philosophy. Unified mobile and 
web dashboards deliver self-serve functionality, instant 
onboarding and dynamic visibility across the enterprise. 
The design architecture prioritises speed, simplicity and 
accessibility — enabling employees, vendors and partners 
to transact, track and manage financial workflows from 
any device.
FY 2025–26 marked the transition from AI 
experimentation to enterprise-wide deployment. Artificial 
intelligence is now embedded across both internal 
engineering operations and customer-facing solutions.
Internally, AI-assisted software development has 
transformed product engineering. The development 
framework, built on Claude Code and the Anthropic 
developer ecosystem, enables engineering teams to 
compress build cycles, automate testing workflows and 
accelerate feature deployment. The technical architecture 
that enables this compression combines AI-assisted code 
generation, automated quality assurance, and modular 
deployment pipelines, allowing features to move from 
concept to production in a fraction of the time historically 
required.
Externally, Agentic AI workflows now automate 
complex enterprise finance processes. Autonomous 
invoice reconciliation runs without human intervention, 
matching purchase orders, invoices and payment records 
across systems. Real-time policy enforcement flags spend 
that falls outside approved parameters at the point of 
transaction, before processing. AI-driven tax compliance 
identifies anomalies in TDS and GST filings, reducing 
manual review cycles and strengthening audit readiness.
A Human-in-the-Loop model governs all high-stakes 
financial environments. The AI handles pattern 
recognition, anomaly detection and routine decision-
making at speed; human oversight is applied at defined 
thresholds where the financial or compliance risk warrants 
manual review. This approach ensures that automation 
accelerates the workflow without removing accountability 
from the process.

card programme with AU Small 
Finance Bank, extending distribution 
into the consumer credit segment. 
An agreement with Euronet further 
extends the distribution architecture 
into payments infrastructure.
These partnerships are force 
multipliers. They convert Zaggle’s 
product capability into market access 
without proportional increases in 
sales and marketing expenditure.
Every transaction on the platform 
generates spend data. The strategic 
objective is to convert that data 
from a byproduct into a revenue-
generating asset. The pathway runs 
through analytics, benchmarking, 
predictive intelligence and, over 
time, advisory services built on 
anonymised, aggregated enterprise 
spend patterns. AI is central to this 
pathway, compressing the time 
between raw transaction data 
and actionable insight, so clients 
move from reviewing historical 
spend to acting on near-real-time 
recommendations.
This is the highest-margin 
opportunity in the portfolio. 
Data monetisation incurs near-
zero incremental cost once the 
intelligence infrastructure is in place, 
and it deepens the platform’s value 
to the client, making switching costs 
structural rather than contractual.
Expand Cross-Border And Embedded Finance
Drive Growth Through Disciplined 
Acquisition And Innovation
The international payments infrastructure described in the 
Expanding Footprint section creates the foundation. The 
strategic objective is to layer embedded financial services, 
namely lending, insurance, credit and forex, onto that 
foundation, serving both Indian enterprises operating 
globally and, over time, international enterprises entering 
the Indian market.
The cross-border opportunity extends beyond corporate 
treasury: the fleet market alone represents an addressable 
market of ₹79,000 crore in India, and forex and remittance 
flows continue to grow as Indian businesses and 
individuals increase their cross-border activity. Separately, 
on the embedded finance side, BBPS-based utility 
payment automation opens an adjacent domestic market 
for enterprises managing recurring operational spend, 
extending the embedded finance layer beyond credit and 
insurance into everyday recurring payments.
Acquisitions remain a core strategic lever, governed by the 
same discipline the Chairman described in his statement: 
will this asset multiply inside the network, or will it simply 
add to the portfolio? The strategic objective is to acquire 
capabilities that accelerate innovation, unlock cross-sell 
pathways and strengthen the AI and embedded finance 
layers of the platform.
Alongside inorganic growth, the product innovation engine continues to 
expand the platform’s organic capabilities. The combination of acquisition-
led capability and innovation-led evolution is designed to build a revenue 
architecture built for long-term, sustainable scale. That is the architectural 
destination, and every strategic allocation is calibrated to reach it.

Our Environment Commitment
Sustainability at Zaggle is a natural consequence of what we have built. As an AI-enabled, cloud-native SaaS-and-
fintech platform, we start from a structural advantage: no physical branches, no legacy infrastructure to power down, 
and no paper-heavy processes to digitise, because we were never built around them in the first place.
FY 2025-26 was the year that advantage compounded at scale. Millions of transactions moved through UPI, prepaid 
and credit cards, and automated accounts payable workflows — each one a transaction that didn’t need a paper trail, a 
plastic form factor, or a carbon-intensive manual process behind it. This is not incidental to what Zoyer, ZIP and Save do; 
it is a part of how they are designed. Efficiency and a lighter environmental footprint arrive together, by construction, 
not as a trade-off we managed after the fact.
We have extended that same discipline to how we run our own workplace. Hybrid working models keep commute-
related emissions down. LED lighting and conscious energy practices run through our offices. Single-use materials have 
been minimised wherever we have had the choice. And underneath all of it, our technology stack sits on shared, elastic 
cloud infrastructure, capacity that scales up and down with demand.

 2.	 STATE OF AFFAIRS AND COMPANY’S PERFORMANCE
	
The Company has recorded total revenue of ₹18,528.12 million during the year 2025-26 as against ₹13,026.46 million in 
the previous year 2024-25, recording a quantum jump of over 42.23% in the total revenue. The net profit after provision 
for tax is ₹1328.55 million during the year 2025-26 as against net profit after tax of ₹ 874.80 million in the previous 
year 2024-25.
	
Your Directors are optimistic about Company’s business and hopeful of better performance with increased revenue in the 
current financial year.
	
Business Performance
	
Zaggle is one of the first home-grown new age SaaS fintech companies listed in India, with a mission to digitize spends 
through automated workflows. We operate in a segment where we interact and interface with our Customers (i.e., businesses) 
and end Users (i.e., employees, channel partners & vendors) and are among a small number of uniquely positioned players 
with a diversified offering of fintech products and services, having one of the largest number of issued payment instruments 
(Prepaid Cards & Commercial Credit Cards) in India in partnership with our banking partners. We operate through the 
following key business segments:
	
Propel: a corporate SaaS platform for channel rewards and incentives, employee rewards and recognition.
	
Save: a SaaS-based platform and a mobile application 
to offer expense management solution for businesses 
facilitating digitised employee reimbursements and 
tax benefits.
	
Zoyer: an integrated data driven, SaaS invoice to pay 
platform with embedded automated finance capabilities.
	
During the year under review, the Company has delivered 
robust growth across all segments.
	
Emerging Products
	
The Company has introduced Zatix, empowering 
businesses with complete control over spends through 
a unified dashboard for corporate cards, and ZIP, 
simplifying international payments with full compliance 
and transparency. 
	
With the recent acquisition of Rivpe Technology Private 
Limited (now rebranded as Zagg.Money), the Company 
has established its presence in the Retail Cards segment, 
backed by a strong pipeline and go-to-market strategy. 
	
The company is developing an AI-driven platform 
to automate ITR filing workflows, simplifying client 
onboarding and creating a seamless experience. offering 
automated ITR filing workflows that make the process 
seamless and simplify client onboarding. 
	
With Greenedge acquisition, Company has strengthened 
foothold 
in 
Bank 
Loyalty 
Programmes, 
opening 
up prospective revenue growth through multiple 
partnerships currently in the pipeline.
	
To its list of City Gas Distribution (CGD) partners, the 
company added Megha City Gas Distribution, Adani 
Total Gas Limited, and IRM Energy, further strengthening 
its fleet business and expanding its revenue potential 
across a wider network of fuel and gas distribution 
touchpoints.
	
Corporates and Users added
	
The Company catered to 3915 Customers in Financial 
Year 2025-2026 compared to 3455 customers in 
financial year 2024-2025. The number of users grew to 
3.90 Mn in Financial Year 2025-2026 from 3.28 Mn in 
previous financial year 2024-2025.
	
Banking and Network Partnerships
	
Zaggle today are partner with 19 banks and 3 networks 
– Visa, Mastercard and Rupay. Further to this, Company 
has deepened its partnership with Mastercard by 
signing a seven-year customer business agreement 
for Mastercard Premium Foreign Currency co-branded 
prepaid cards, further strengthening the company's forex 
offering. Alongside this, Zaggle has also partnered with 
Mastercard to launch and promote co-branded domestic 
prepaid cards on the Mastercard network. As part of 
this expanded relationship, Mastercard will offer spend-
linked incentives to Zaggle for introducing customers to 
credit cards and other value-added financial services on 
the Mastercard network.
	
The Company has also signed a bundled partnership 
with AU Small Finance Bank covering three areas: 
launching a co-branded retail credit card powered by 
a personalized recommendation engine with TPAP 
integration, issuing corporate credit cards to Zaggle's 
corporate customer base, and launching a co-branded 
prepaid card solution powered by the Zatix platform for 
Zaggle's corporate clients.
	
In addition, Zaggle has entered into reseller partnerships 
with IDFC First Bank and Standard Chartered Bank. 
Separately, the Company has signed a seven-year 
partnership with Visa Worldwide, under which Visa will 
offer spend-linked incentives to Zaggle to launch and 
promote co-branded domestic prepaid cards on the 
Visa network.
	
Business Partnerships
	
Zaggle has strengthened its Smart Employee Purchase 
Programme (Smart EPP) by onboarding Jio Credit as a 
leasing partner, while its partnership with Tata Capital 
adds greater financial flexibility, giving employees access 
to more attractive leasing options for their purchases.

y
Enhanced decision-making: Board diversity 
combines individuals with unique backgrounds, 
experiences, 
and 
perspectives, 
fostering 
robust decision-making. By embracing diverse 
viewpoints, boards can avoid groupthink, drive 
innovation, and make informed choices.
 
y
Enhanced problem-solving: Diverse boards 
tackle complex problems more effectively 
by 
leveraging 
varied 
backgrounds 
and 
experiences. Multiple perspectives lead to 
enhanced problem-solving, driving better 
outcomes for the organization.
 
y
Improved corporate governance: Diverse 
boards with varied skills, knowledge, and 
experiences provide comprehensive oversight, 
addressing conflicts, promoting transparency, 
and ensuring accountability – ultimately 
enhancing corporate governance practices.
 
y
Better understanding of customers and 
markets: Diverse boards bring valuable 
insights into India’s varied cultures, languages, 
and 
consumer 
preferences, 
enabling 
companies to tailor products, services, and 
marketing strategies to effectively target 
diverse customer groups.
 
y
Increased creativity and innovation: Diversity 
sparks creativity and innovation by bringing 
together 
varied 
perspectives, 
fostering 
openness, 
collaboration, 
and 
inclusivity. 
Different viewpoints challenge norms, drive 
fresh ideas, and lead to innovative solutions.
 
y
Mitigation of biases: Diverse boards can 
help 
mitigate 
unconscious 
biases 
and 
promote fairness and equity. By ensuring 
representation 
from 
different 
genders, 
ethnicities, age groups, and backgrounds, 
boards can counterbalance any inherent 
biases and ensure a more equitable and 
inclusive decision-making process.
 
y
Improved reputation and stakeholder trust: 
Diverse boards foster a positive reputation for 
inclusivity and social responsibility, enhancing 
brand image, attracting diverse talent, and 
building stakeholder trust. Benefits include 
improved 
decision-making, 
governance, 
innovation, 
problem-solving, 
market 
understanding, and reputation – driving long-
term success and sustainability.

advantages, including improved decision-making,

corporate 
governance, 
increased 
creativity and innovation, better problem solving, 
understanding of diverse markets, improved 
reputation, and the mitigation of biases. These 
benefits contribute to the long-term success

Internal Audit and Control System:
	
Internal audit and control systems play a crucial role 
in ensuring the efficient and effective operation of 
organizations across various sectors. Internal audit 
refers to the independent and objective examination 
of an organization’s activities, processes, and 
controls to assess their adequacy, reliability, and 
compliance with relevant laws, regulations, and 
internal policies. The primary objective of internal 
audit is to provide assurance to management and 
stakeholders that risks are identified, managed, and 
mitigated appropriately.
	
Internal audit encompasses a wide range of 
activities, including evaluating the effectiveness of 
internal controls, identifying areas of improvement, 
assessing operational efficiency, detecting fraud 
and irregularities, and ensuring compliance with 
legal and regulatory requirements. By conducting 
regular audits, internal auditors help organizations 
identify potential weaknesses in their systems and 
processes, allowing management to take proactive 
measures to address them.
	
Control systems, on the other hand, refer to the 
policies, procedures, and practices put in place by 
management to safeguard assets, ensure accurate 
financial reporting, and promote operational 
efficiency. These control systems aim to mitigate 
risks and provide reasonable assurance that the 
organization’s objectives are achieved.
	
The internal audit function is responsible for 
evaluating the design and effectiveness of these 
control systems. Internal auditors assess whether 
the controls are properly designed to mitigate 
risks and whether they are operating effectively 
in practice. They conduct tests and reviews to 
identify control gaps, weaknesses, or deviations 
from established policies and procedures. Based 
on their findings, they provide recommendations to 
management for enhancing controls and improving 
processes, thus helping the organization operate in 
a more efficient and risk-aware manner.
	
Effective internal audit and control systems 
contribute to better governance, risk management, 
and internal controls within an organization. They 
provide management and stakeholders with 
confidence that risks are managed appropriately, 
financial information is reliable, and operations 
are conducted with integrity. By continuously 
monitoring and evaluating controls, internal audit 
helps organizations stay ahead of emerging risks, 
adapt to changing business environments, and 
enhance overall performance and accountability.
	
The Company has an Audit Committee consisting 
of three Independent Directors and one Executive 
Director. The Audit Committee of the Board of 
Directors and Statutory Auditors are periodically 
apprised of the internal audit findings and corrective 
actions taken. The Audit Committee of the Board of 
Directors reviews the adequacy and effectiveness of 
internal control system and suggests improvements, 
if any, for strengthening them.

25.	 RISK MANAGEMENT
	
Pursuant to Section 134(3)(n) of the Companies Act, 
2013 and Regulation 17(9) of Securities and Exchange 
Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, the Company has 
formulated and adopted a Policy on Risk Management 
and Procedure. The Risk Management policy of the 
Company outlines a framework for identification of 
internal and external risks specifically faced by the 
Company, in particular including financial, operational, 
sectoral, information, cyber security risks, or any other 
risk as may be determined by the Committee; measures 
for risk mitigation including systems and processes for 
internal control of identified risks; and Business continuity 
plan. Risk is an integral part of the Company’s business, 
and sound risk management is critical to the success of 
the organization. The Company has adequate internal 
financial control systems and procedures to combat the 
risk. The risk management procedure is reviewed by the 
Audit Committee and Board of Directors on a regular 
basis at the time of review of the quarterly financial 
results of the Company.
	
Furthermore, pursuant to the requirement of Regulation 
21 of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 
2015, the Company has constituted a Risk Management 
Committee (RMC), consisting of Board members of 
the Company.
	
The Company has in place a Risk Management framework 
to identify, evaluate business risks and challenges across 
the Company both at corporate level as also separately 
for each business division.
	
The Company has in place a mechanism to identify, 
assess, monitor and mitigate various risks to key business 
objectives. Major risks identified by the businesses 
and functions are systematically addressed through 
mitigating actions on a continuing basis. The Company’s 
internal control encompasses various managements 
systems, structures of organization, standard and code 
of conduct which all put together help in managing the 
risks associated with the Company.
	
Based on the assessment undertaken by the Management 
and the Risk Management Committee, no material risks 
were identified during the year under review that, in 
the opinion of the Board of Directors, may threaten the 
existence of the Company. The Company continues to 
monitor emerging and evolving risks and undertakes 
appropriate measures to mitigate their potential impact. 
The key risks and mitigation measures are discussed 
in detail in the Management Discussion and Analysis 
Report forming part of this Annual Report.

A brief on types of customers
The Company serves a diverse customer base comprising large 
enterprises, mid-sized businesses, SMEs, government organizations, 
startups and educational institutions across various industries. Its solutions 
cater to corporate finance teams, HR departments, procurement teams, 
supply chain and employees by providing digital spend management, 
device leasing, travel expenses, procure to pay, tax solutions, golf 
services, employee benefits, corporate expense management, rewards 
& recognition, prepaid cards, commercial credit card, forex, fleet 
management, retail credit cards, UPI services, utility payments and 
payment automation solutions. The Company also partners with 19 
banks, financial institutions, merchants and channel partners to deliver 
integrated fintech solutions, enabling businesses to streamline financial 
operations while enhancing employee and customer experiences.

on prevention of bribery, facilitation payments and kickbacks, gifts and hospitality, third-party dealings, procurement, conflicts 
of interest, internal controls, compliance training and reporting of concerns.

direct or indirect. It also establishes clear procedures for procurement, third-party due diligence, political and charitable

Officer to oversee adherence to the policy and ensure periodic monitoring, review, and corrective action where necessary.

all the jurisdictions in which it operates.

The Zaggle Intelligence Flywheel
Zaggle's growth model is not a 
single loop but a four-sided network 
connecting corporates, partners, 
merchants, and employees/users/
SMBs - each node reinforcing the 
others rather than growing in 
isolation.

distinct, compounding revenue 
streams: SaaS fees from corporates, 
programme fees from partners, 
merchant commission from 
merchants, and VAS fees from 
employees/users/SMBs - meaning 
growth in any one node expands 
Zaggle's monetisation surface across 
all the others, rather than simply 
adding linear revenue.

at the cost of efficiency: customer 
acquisition cost remains under 5% 
of revenue and churn stays below 
1.5%, evidence that each new node 
added to the network makes the next 
one cheaper to acquire and easier to 
retain.

Income
Revenue from operations rose 46.32% 
to C 19,076.46 million from C 13,037.57 
million, driven by broad-based 
growth across spend management, 
benefits, rewards, vendor payments 
and financial automation.
Propel and gift cards: Revenue 
grew 53.41% to C 11,074.07 million 
from C 7,218.48 million, supported 
by a larger rewards ecosystem, 
higher volumes and wider adoption. 
Platform users increased to 3.90 
million from 3.30 million, while the 
customer base expanded to 3,915 
from 3,455. 
Programme fee: Income increased 
37.87% to C 7,523.35 million from 
C 5,456.41 million, reflecting higher 
transaction volumes, increased 
customer activity and greater spend 
across the platform, supported by the 
Save and Zoyer solutions. 
Platform, SaaS and service fee: 
Income increased 32.08% to C 479.04 
million from C 362.68 million, driven 
by higher adoption and utilisation 
of the Company’s technology-led 
solutions. 
Other income: Increased 41.95% to 
C 380.03 million from C 267.73 million, 
supported by higher treasury income 
from capital raises and a one-time 
gain on remeasurement of the 
TaxSpanner associate following an 
additional stake. 
Expenses
Total expenses rose 45.60% to 
C 17,649.04 million from C 12,121.96 
million, broadly in line with the 
growth in business volumes and 
continued investments in technology, 
products and capabilities. 
Importantly, expenses as a 
percentage of total income improved 
to 90.7% from 91.1%, reflecting 
operating leverage. 
Cost of point redemption and gift 
cards: Rose 54.91% to C 10,504.73 
million in FY 2025-26 from C 6,781.00 
million in FY 2024-25, in line with 
the growth in Propel and higher 
redemption volumes. 
Employee benefits expense: 
Increased 5.51% to C 704.19 million 
from C 667.41 million, reflecting 
continued investments in technology, 
product, sales and customer success 
capabilities. 
Finance costs: Declined 30.37% to 
C 53.30 million from C 76.55 million, 
supported by refinancing and 
repayment of borrowings. 
Depreciation and amortisation: 
Increased 149.29% to C 368.80 million 
from C 147.94 million, reflecting 
higher investments in technology 
and product capabilities. 
Other expenses: Increased 35.44% 
to C 6,002.95 million from C 4,432.06 
million, reflecting higher business 
volumes and continued investments 
across incentives, technology and 
business development. 
Profitability
Profit before tax (PBT) increased 
56.36% to C 1,851.57 million from 
C 1,184.17 million, while profit 
after tax (PAT) increased 57.86% 
to C 1,387.55 million from C 878.98 
million. The improvement was driven 
by strong revenue growth, operating 
leverage and cost discipline, even as 
the Company continued investing in 
product, technology, acquisitions and 
people.

effective oversight of performance.

story. As the platform has scaled, 
so has our conviction that business 
outcomes are inseparable from 
how well our people strategy tracks 
the Company’s evolving needs - 
every structural decision on hiring, 
development and leadership is made 
with this alignment in mind.
Building a workplace that is inclusive 
and genuinely rewarding to work in 
has been a deliberate priority rather 
than a byproduct of growth. That 
commitment extends to the whole 
person: performance support sits 
alongside emotional and physical 
wellbeing, backed by consistent 
investment in health, safety and 
workplace practices designed to 
hold up as the organisation scales. 
Financial wellness has become part of 
this picture too, with regular sessions 
that help employees build a better

and risk management, extending the 
same spend-management thinking 
we bring to our clients into our 
employees’ own financial lives.

into ongoing development - skill-

appraisal framework keeps incentives 
tied to objective, measurable

judgment.

1. BOARD OF DIRECTORS
The Board of Directors is the highest governance body 
constituted to oversee the Company’s overall functioning. 
The responsibility of the Board is to provide strategic 
guidance to the Company, to ensure effective monitoring 
of the management and to be accountable to the Company 
and the shareholders. The meetings of the Board of Directors 
are held generally at the Company’s Registered Office at 
Hyderabad and are scheduled well in advance. In case of 
business exigencies or urgency of matters, resolutions are 
passed by circulation. Information relating to the business, 
operations and risks affecting the Company is regularly 
placed before the Board / Committee for its consideration 
apart from information as mentioned in Part A of Schedule II 
of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations 
and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The Board 
regularly reviews the compliance reports of all laws applicable 
to the Company.

Board has specific obligations to fulfil.
	
The primary role of the Board is to act as a fiduciary for the 
Company, representing the interests of its shareholders 
and stakeholders. The Board is responsible for providing 
strategic guidance and setting the overall direction and 
objectives of the Company. It must exercise independent 
judgment and act in the best interests of the Company 
while considering the interests of all stakeholders.
	
The responsibilities of the Board include:
1)	
Corporate Governance: The Board is accountable 
for maintaining high standards of corporate 
governance, ensuring transparency, and adhering 
to legal and regulatory requirements. It must 
establish and monitor systems of internal control 
and risk management to safeguard the Company’s 
assets and reputation.
2)	
Strategy and Planning: The Board plays a crucial 
role in formulating the Company’s strategic plans, 
assessing risks, and identifying opportunities. It 
approves annual budgets, business plans, and 
major investment decisions. It also monitors the 
implementation of strategies and evaluates their 
effectiveness.
3)	
Oversight and Monitoring: The Board has a duty 
to oversee the Company’s management, ensuring 
that it operates in a responsible and ethical manner. 
It appoints and evaluates the performance of 
key executives, including the CEO. The Board 
also reviews financial statements, internal audit 
reports, and compliance with legal and regulatory 
obligations.
4)	
Stakeholder 
Management: 
The 
Board 
must 
consider the interests of various stakeholders, 
including shareholders, employees, customers, 
suppliers, and the community. It should foster 
effective communication and engagement with 
stakeholders and address their concerns.
5)	
Risk Management: The Board is responsible 
for identifying and managing risks faced by 
the Company. It should establish effective risk 
management policies and procedures, ensure 
appropriate insurance coverage, and regularly 
review the effectiveness of risk mitigation measures.
6)	
Compliance and Disclosures: The Board ensures 
compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and 
codes of conduct. It oversees the disclosure of 
accurate and timely information to shareholders 
and other stakeholders, maintaining transparency 
and fairness. Under Section 166 of the Companies 
Act, 2013, the Board has a fiduciary duty to act in 
good faith, exercise due care, and act in the best 
interests of the Company. It should promote the 
Company’s objectives, preserve its assets, and 
ensure its long-term success. The Act emphasizes 
the duty of directors to act honestly, responsibly, 
and with reasonable diligence, using their skills and 
knowledge for the benefit of the Company.
	
In conclusion, the Board of Directors plays a 
critical role in the governance and management 
of a Company. It has various responsibilities and 
duties, including strategic planning, oversight, 
risk management, compliance, and stakeholder 
management.

Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and Section 166 
of the Companies Act, 2013, provide a framework 
for the Board to fulfill its obligations and ensure the

Policy for Prevention of Insider Trading
	
The Company has adopted a Code of Conduct to 
Regulate, Monitor and Report Trading by Designated 
Persons and their Immediate Relatives (Policy/
Code) for Regulating, Monitoring and Reporting of 
Trades by Designated Persons’ and their immediate 
relatives in accordance with the Securities and 
Exchange Board of India (Prohibition of Insider 
Trading) Regulations, 2015. The Company is having 
in place the required IT infrastructure for maintaining 
Structured Digital Database and for monitoring 
the insider trading activities as per the applicable 
Regulations of Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 
2015. The Policy is applicable to Promoters, 
Member of Promoter’s Group, all Directors, 
designated persons (and their immediate relatives) 
and third parties such as auditors, consultants etc. 
who are expected to have access to unpublished 
price sensitive information relating to the Company. 
The trading window of the Company is closed from 
the first day of the every quarter and it opens after 
48 hours of the declaration of financial results and 
on occurrence of any material events as per the 
code. The Audit Committee of the Company shall 
review compliance with the provisions of these 
regulations at least once in a financial year and 
shall verify that the systems for internal control are 
adequate and are operating effectively.
	
The Company has also formulated ‘Code of 
Practices and Procedures for Fair Disclosure of 
Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (UPSI)’ in 
compliance with the Securities and Exchange Board 
of India (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 
2015. The Company also has a whistle-blower 
policy to make employees aware of such policy to 
enable employees to report instances of leak of 
UPSI and a separate procedure for enquiry in case 
of leak of UPSI is also in place. The same is also available on the Company’s website https://ir.zaggle.in/wp-content/

Performance evaluation criteria of Independent Directors:
	
One of the key functions of the Committee is to monitor and review the board evaluation framework. The Board is 
committed to assessing its own performance as a Board in order to identify its strengths and areas in which it may improve 
its functioning.
	
The Board works with the Nomination and Remuneration Committee to lay down the evaluation criteria for the performance 
of executive / non-executive / independent directors. The questionnaire is a key part of the process of reviewing the 
functioning and effectiveness of the Board and for identifying possible paths for improvement. Each Board member is 
requested to evaluate the effectiveness of the Board dynamics and relationships, information flow, decision-making of the 
directors, relationship to stakeholders, company performance, company strategy, and the effectiveness of the whole Board 
and its various committees on a scale of one to five. Feedback on each Director is encouraged to be provided as part of the 
questionnaire.

Report on the Audit of the Standalone Financial Statements
Opinion
We have audited the accompanying standalone financial 
statements of Zaggle Prepaid Ocean Services Limited (“the 
Company”), which comprise the Balance Sheet as at March 
31, 2026, the Statement of Profit and Loss (including Other 
Comprehensive Income), the Statement of Changes in Equity 
and the Statement of Cash Flows for the year then ended 
and notes to the standalone financial statements, including 
material accounting policy information and other explanatory 
information (hereinafter referred to as the “standalone financial 
statements”).
In our opinion and to the best of our information and according 
to the explanations given to us, the aforesaid standalone 
financial statements give the information required by the 
Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) in the manner so required 
and give a true and fair view in conformity with the Indian 
Accounting Standards prescribed under section 133 of the 
Act, read with Companies (Indian Accounting Standards) 
Rules, 2015, as amended (“Ind  AS”) and other accounting 
principles generally accepted in India, of the state of affairs 
of the Company as at March 31, 2026 and its profit (including 
other comprehensive loss), changes in equity and its cash 
flows for the year ended on that date.
Basis for Opinion
We conducted our audit of the standalone financial statements 
in accordance with the Standards on Auditing (SAs) specified 
under section 143(10) of the Act. Our responsibilities 
under those SAs are further described in the ‘Auditor’s 
Responsibilities for the Audit of the Standalone Financial 
Statements’ section of our report. We are independent of the 
Company in accordance with the Code of Ethics issued by 
the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India together with 
the ethical requirements that are relevant to our audit of the 
standalone financial statements under the provisions of the 
Act and the Rules thereunder, and we have fulfilled our other 
ethical responsibilities in accordance with these requirements 
and the Code of Ethics. We believe that the audit evidence we 
have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis 
for our opinion.
Key Audit Matter
Key audit matter is the matter that, in our professional judgment, 
was of most significance in our audit of the standalone financial 
statements of the current year. This matter was addressed in 
the context of our audit of the standalone financial statements 
as a whole, and in forming our opinion thereon, and we do not 
provide a separate opinion on this matter. We have determined 
the matter described below to be the key audit matter to be 
communicated in our report.
Revenue Recognition [Refer note 2.2 (A) of Standalone 
Financial Statements]:
Revenue is a key performance measure for the Company. 
Revenue of the Company mainly comprise of program 
fees, fees income/SaaS income and sales of propel gift 
cards vouchers.
Revenue is recognised as per the terms of the contract with 
the respective customers and when it meets the recognition 
criteria as per Ind AS 115 on “Revenue from contracts 
with customers”.
There exists a risk of revenue not being recognised in 
proportion to the service performed by the Company. Further, 
revenue may also be recorded in an incorrect period or on a 
basis which is inconsistent with the contractual terms agreed 
with the customers.
In view of the above factors and given that the Company and its 
stakeholders focus on revenue as a key performance indicator, 
we have determined Revenue to be a key audit matter.
How the Key Audit Matter was addressed in our audit:
1.	
Evaluated the appropriateness of the revenue recognition 
accounting policies of the Company with the principles 
of Indian Accounting standard 115 - 'Revenue from 
contracts with customer' ('Ind AS 115').
2.	
Evaluated the design, implementation and tested the 
operating effectiveness of the relevant key controls with 
respect to revenue recognition.
3.	
Performed Analytical procedures on revenue recognised 
during the year to identify and inquire on unusual 
variances, if any and getting the reasons for variances 
confirmed from the management of the Company.
4.	
Verified completeness and existence assertion by 
performing substantive testing on selected samples 
of revenue transactions recorded during the year by 
testing the underlying documents including contracts, 
invoices, gift voucher delivery communications and 
customer receipts, wherever applicable and obtaining 
independent balance confirmation from the customers at 
the balance sheet date.
5.	
Verified cut off assertion by reviewing the Company’s 
revenue recognition policies, testing samples of revenue 
transactions near the end of the reporting period and 
verified supporting documents to verify that the revenue 
is recorded in corrected accounting period.
6.	
Tested on a sample basis, manual journal entries relating 
to revenues to identify and inquire on unusual items, if any.
7.	
Assessed the adequacy and appropriateness of the 
disclosures made in the financial statements to verify 
they are accurate, complete, and comply with the 
requirements of Ind AS 115 - 'Revenue from contracts 
with customer'.

Report on the Internal Financial Controls with reference 
to standalone financial statements under Clause (i) of 
Sub-section 3 of Section 143 of the Act
Opinion
We have audited the internal financial controls with reference 
to standalone financial statements of Zaggle Prepaid Ocean 
Services Limited (“the Company”) as of March 31, 2026, 
in conjunction with our audit of the standalone financial 
statements of the Company for the year ended on that date.
In our opinion, to the best of our information and according to 
the explanations given to us, the Company has, in all material 
respects, an adequate internal financial controls with reference 
to standalone financial statements and such internal financial 
controls with reference to standalone financial statements 
were operating effectively as at March 31, 2026, based on 
the internal financial controls with reference to standalone 
financial statements criteria established by the Company 
considering the essential components of internal control stated 
in the Guidance Note on Audit of Internal Financial Controls 
Over Financial Reporting (“the Guidance Note”) issued by the 
Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI).
Management’s and Board of Directors’ Responsibility 
for Internal Financial Controls
The Company’s Management and the Board of Directors are 
responsible for establishing and maintaining internal financial 
controls based on the internal control with reference to 
standalone financial statements criteria established by the 
Company considering the essential components of internal 
control stated in the Guidance Note issued by the ICAI. These 
responsibilities include the design, implementation and 
maintenance of adequate internal financial controls that were 
operating effectively for ensuring the orderly and efficient 
conduct of its business, including adherence to Company’s 
policies, the safeguarding of its assets, the prevention and 
detection of frauds and errors, the accuracy and completeness 
of the accounting records, and the timely preparation of 
reliable financial information, as required under the Act.
Auditor’s Responsibility
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on the Company's 
internal financial controls with reference to standalone financial 
statements based on our audit. We conducted our audit in 
accordance with the Guidance Note issued by ICAI and the 
Standard on Auditing prescribed under section 143(10) of the 
Act, to the extent applicable to an audit of internal financial 
controls with reference to standalone financial statements. 
Those Standards and the Guidance Note require that we 
comply with ethical requirements and plan and perform the 
audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether adequate 
internal financial controls with reference to standalone 
financial statements was established and maintained and if 
such controls operated effectively in all material respects.
Our audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit 
evidence about the adequacy of the internal financial controls 
with reference to standalone financial statements and their 
operating effectiveness. Our audit of internal financial controls 
with reference to standalone financial statements included 
obtaining an understanding of internal financial controls with 
reference to standalone financial statements, assessing the risk 
that a material weakness exists, and testing and evaluating the 
design and operating effectiveness of internal control based 
on the assessed risk. The procedures selected depend on the 
auditor’s judgement, including the assessment of the risks of 
material misstatement of the standalone financial statements, 
whether due to fraud or error.
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is 
sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit 
opinion on the Company’s internal financial controls with 
reference to standalone financial statements.
Meaning of Internal Financial Controls with reference 
to Financial Statements
A Company's internal financial control with reference to 
financial statements is a process designed to provide 
reasonable assurance regarding the reliability of financial 
reporting and the preparation of financial statements for 
external purposes in accordance with generally accepted 
accounting principles. A company's internal financial control 
with reference to financial statements includes those 
policies and procedures that (1) pertain to the maintenance 
of records that, in reasonable detail, accurately and fairly 
reflect the transactions and dispositions of the assets of the 
company; (2) provide reasonable assurance that transactions 
are recorded as necessary to permit preparation of financial 
statements in accordance with generally accepted accounting 
principles, and that receipts and expenditures of the company 
are being made only in accordance with authorizations of 
management and directors of the company; and (3) provide 
reasonable assurance regarding prevention or timely 
detection of unauthorized acquisition, use, or disposition of 
the company's assets that could have a material effect on the 
financial statements.
Inherent Limitations of Internal Financial Controls 
with reference to Financial Statements
Because of the inherent limitations of internal financial 
controls with reference to financial statements, including the 
possibility of collusion or improper management override of 
controls, material misstatements due to error or fraud may 
occur and not be detected. Also, projections of any evaluation 
of the internal financial controls with reference to financial 
statements to future periods are subject to the risk that the 
internal financial control with reference to financial statements 
may become inadequate because of changes in conditions, or 
that the degree of compliance with the policies or procedures 
may deteriorate.

(v)	
Measurement of fair values
	
Accounting 
polices 
and 
disclosures 
require 
measurement of fair value for financial assets and 
financial liabilities.
	
Fair value is the price that would be received to sell 
an asset or paid to transfer a liability in an orderly 
transaction between market participants at the 
measurement date. The fair value measurement is 
based on the presumption that the transaction to sell 
the asset or transfer the liability takes place either:
 - 	
In the principal market for the asset or liability or
 - 	
In the absence of a principal market, in the 
most advantageous market for the asset 
or liability.
	
The principal or the most advantageous market 
must be accessible by the Company. The fair 
value of an asset or a liability is measured using 
the assumptions that market participants would 
use when pricing the asset or liability, assuming 
that market participants act in their economic 
best interest.
	
The Company uses valuation techniques that are 
appropriate in the circumstances and for which 
sufficient data is available to measure fair value, 
maximising the use of relevant observable inputs 
and minimising the use of unobservable inputs.
	
Fair values are categorised into different levels in a 
fair value hierarchy based on the inputs used in the 
valuation techniques as follows:
	
Level 1: Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active 
markets for identical assets or liabilities.
	
Level 2: Inputs other than quoted prices included in 
Level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, 
either directly (i.e. as prices) or indirectly (i.e. derived 
from prices).
	
Level 3: Inputs for the asset or liability that 
are not based on observable market data 
(unobservable inputs).
	
The Company recognizes transfers between levels 
of the fair value hierarchy at the end of the reporting 
period during which the change has occurred.
	
Further information about the assumptions made 
in the measuring fair values is included in the 
following notes:
	
- note36 - Financial instruments.
